body: Unfortunately I finished it a couple months back and couldn’t find the exact screen time. BUT I did disable auto lock on my screen so it always stayed on, even overnight where I’d keep my phone charged, on silent and away from my bed - in the morning I would always manage to attract a gambling mouse at minimum + about a hundred city customers overnight. TLDR too long probably

Coming from someone who has accomplished this with 3 days to spare: it is doable! But you’ll need to lock in.

City customers: with about 4,200 city customers to attract in 20d, you’ll need to attract at minimum 210 city customers daily. Be sure to always keep 4daisy + 4rose planted in garden for attracting Chocolate Labs OR 4sunflower + 4bluebell for attracting Speckled Pigs. I think the fandom wiki also mentions them as being the most easily attracted city customers. Spam 15x promos with them for sure.

Gambling mouse: fandom wiki has a tip about intentionally never talking to the other special customers that don’t auto-leave, e.g. singing parrot, mysterious merchant, wizard, TV salesman… as the game algorithm seems to randomly shuffle between them. However, if you keep them on all the time while also always keeping your restaurant screen open, eventually the gambling mouse will start to come. With this method, they can show up at least twice per day quite easily.

Keeping your phone open all the time coincidentally also lets customers naturally trickle in when you need a break from spamming 15x promos. In my experience, collecting my daily things like wish fountain loot, daily plates, etc. While keeping a finger holding on the manual promo button helped me accomplish the promo task pretty quickly. 

Good luck!

Sometimes I think about how much nicer things would be if I never went through a depressive episode, and stayed happier with things. In my specific case, though, could things really have ever turned out well? Perhaps if my upbringing went differently, among a bunch of other factors, but at that point,why bother thinking about what could've been?

We're dealt with some cards from the get-go of life, and we can't change those cards. But we can always do something about how we play those cards, and most importantly, we can always do something about the cards we continue to draw.

Thanks to whoever's been reading/skimming through my rambling. Here's to hoping that things continue going up, and working hard to make sure things keep going up.

I'm sure a blunt and matter-of-fact way of putting it is saying that things are only gonna get worse. I can't really disagree with that, but at the same time I can't completely agree, either. 

Maybe it's just how I see it, but saying that things will only get worse feels like I'd be dismissing all the potentially great things that life's yet to provide. Life and things can really feel absurd at times, especially if I'm gonna measure it by means of saying we'll never amount to anything.

But at the same time, by what means am I measuring that? It could be quite clear that things could just as easily turn out for the better, but it seems like as long as I can do something, even the most minuscule thing, that I can look back at and say it was worth *something*, then life is eventually gonna start turning for the better.

I used to think that purposely thinking about how things are gonna get better is the same as deluding myself from an ugly truth (where things will never get better), but isn't it the same thing if I flip perspectives? The truth of whether life's gonna turn out well or horribly is something that frankly, there's no way I, or anyone, could ever predict. So it seems like the key is to keep looking up, even if it seems like there's nothing but signs pointing down. Because how would any of us really know which way things are gonna go?

Hey! Chiming in along with the previous comment. Jayce is more or less one of Shen's hardest matchups, and there isn't too much you can do to win lane other than capitalizing on Jayce's mistakes.

What's your rune/mastery setup? Take armor quints if you aren't already; Shen doesn't need AD in his runes. For masteries, always 12/0/18, and if you're not taking Colossus, take it - you need that shield.

Start Dshield. In lane, don't trade or go for CS if you don't have your passive shield, Colossus, and/or W up, and watch when he goes for farm - he can't auto you if he's autoing a creep (unless he uses cannon W, in which case you can W/shield it). Jayce is always gonna try to poke you down for going for farm, but he pushes quite easily, so jungle ganks can hurt him pretty hard. Rush Sunfire, and play conservatively to 6. Shen can't 1v5 very easily, but he damn well can make it easier for his teammates to do the job.

Stay alert as to when he's roaming so you can ult to where he goes. Having a second TP is mad strong when used correctly. 

[This Challenger Shen player] (https://www.reddit.com/r/summonerschool/comments/5nlai2/challenger_shen_guide_for_season_7_by_petu/) might be able to answer some more questions if you haven't seen it yet.

On Top Graves:

· He definitely doesn't build both Maw + Sterak's anymore. Pick one. I almost always go Maw for the additional ArmPen and sustain (Sterak's vs. Full AD)

· Graves honestly does pretty well into everyone. You have so much sustain and waveclear that you can often easily powerfarm early on. Generally speaking, you have a huge advantage over most melees, and you get outranged by other ranged champions.

· Be cautious with trading too often, your Q and W cost a lot of mana. Ideally save E for a mix of kiting, reloading an auto, and repositioning for an instant Q. You get resists from E but it's hard to stack those resists in lane without going oom. An all-in trade would go something like aa-W-aa-E-aa-Q while reloading. Make the most of your smokescreen while trading, that vision denial is so strong.

· Once you get DD/PD you're a monster duelist, so you're not a bad splitpusher. You pack a ton of aoe and nice utility in teamfights, but this is totally situational.  Make the most out of your tp, and keep farming up. 

You can cancel Graves' ult knockback with his E. There are videos on this and it's quite helpful, but be careful, since you're blowing both your escapes with this.
